Sampled HR@10 and full-catalog HR@10 can reverse model rankings, even in expectation; increasing repetitions does not remove this discrepancy. Small candidate sets also weaken emphasis on top-ranked items. These findings directly caution against interpreting the benchmark’s 99-negative HR@10 as full-catalog quality. Retain the pinned evaluator for selection; use full-catalog validation ranking only as a separately labeled diagnostic on the same users. [Krichene and Rendle](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651).

Recent reproducibility studies support controlled component comparisons. A 2024 sequential-recommendation analysis finds that SASRec versus GRU4Rec conclusions depend strongly on experimental configuration and parameter count. A December 2025 BSARec reproduction reports no clear advantage of signal-processing components over simple residual connections, with padding substantially affecting results. Practical implication: match training budgets and change one component, loss, or sampling strategy at a time. [Sequential reproducibility study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03873), [BSARec reproduction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17442).

Proposed diagnostic validation, rather than an established result from these papers: inject increasing history shuffling, truncation, embedding randomization, and popularity-only scoring; test whether each probe responds to its intended failure. Include repeated unchanged inference and consistent item-ID permutation as invariance controls. Bootstrap paired user-level hit differences within each category, then average the four category differences for macro uncertainty; these intervals condition on the fixed candidates and trained checkpoints. Report probe associations with validation improvements as exploratory, accounting for repeated checkpoint searches. Freeze users, candidates, seeds, and splits; keep corruption experiments isolated from official scoring. Use only observed histories and permitted metadata, without inferring unavailable simulator traits.
